> I think that the `Attempting to use an uninitialized RID` error is caused by the fact that the texture couldn't import, not the cause of the import

That's right, everything is likely caused by the `ERROR: servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp:881 - Condition "p_layers[i]->get_format() != valid_format" is true.` error

I dug through the code a little bit and did some testing.
The reason the `Condition "p_layers[i]->get_format() != valid_format" is true.` error is happening is because the image format is not consistent throughout all of the layers (i.e. layer A has the RGBA8 format, but layer B has the LA8 format).

I did some testing with the default `icon.svg` and found that if I set the compression to lossless and the both the horizontal and vertical slices to 2, it would import correctly and I would be left with all 4 layers. However, when I changed the number of slices to anything greater than 2, it threw the error.

I have no clue why this is happening. In the test with only 2x2, it showed that the entire image had the same format (otherwise it would've thrown the error), but for the 4x4 test that error happened, which means something changed the format.

> ~This appears to be a regression between 4.2.2 and 4.3~ nevermind, my testing methodology was off. I can reproduce in 4.1.4 as well

Have you tested more version than you've mentioned or are those all the ones you've tried

I tested 4.1.4, 4.2.2, 4.3, 4.4.1 and a bunch of 4.3 dev releases when I thought it was a regression. My guess is that this never worked in the first place.
yes, it appears to have never worked in the first place

I did some more testing with an image that doesn't contain any alpha pixels (this is saved as an RGB8). It was able to do as many slices as I wanted (until I hit the built-in limit).

After playing around with it a little bit more, I think the reason why the icon.svg didn't work with more than 2x2 slices (2 horizontal slices and 2 vertical slices) has to do with the fact that the icon.svg has transparent pixels at its corners.

At 2x2 slices, each layer has a corner, and therefore has transparent pixels, so the engine uses RGBA8 format (contains an Alpha). When doing 4x4 slices, the corner layers will still have transparent pixels, resulting in RGBA8 format, but the middle layers don't have the corners, so they don't have transparent pixels, so the engine uses RBG8 format (without an Alpha channel) for those. Thus, the corner layers use RGBA8 format and the middle layers use RGB8 format, resulting in different format, throwing the error.

In [line 379 of resource_importer_layered_texture.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b89c47bb8511433440e5e547afe4459ca3383090/editor/import/resource_importer_layered_texture.cpp#L379) it mentions `Ref<Image> slice = image->get_region(Rect2i(x, y, slice_w, slice_h));`
This line gets a region of the image. It makes a call to [Image::get_region](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b89c47bb8511433440e5e547afe4459ca3383090/core/io/image.cpp#L2845). I believe that the get_region function is what is responsible for converting the RGBA8 format to RGB8 format if it doesn't have any transparent pixels. 

What I don't get is why it doesn't use the format of the original image as the new format.

*Edit: This theory was incorrect*
@Haha64142 Great work, that sounds very likely if we are detecting alpha on a per-layer basis.

So I actually dug into the function more and also did some modifying of the code, and found out that it actually wasn't in the get_region function at all. I found out that the format switch happens at the end of the importing process when the image is saving.

### Solution
You can get the texture to import correctly if you go to project setting, and with the advanced switch on, set `redering/textures/lossless_compression/force_png` setting to true. (You can also search for `force png` and it will pull up the correct option)

**Note:** This will not work with lossy compression

-----------------------------------

The reason why the texture was detecting alpha on a per-layer basis was because it was being saved as a webp image, which detects alpha on a per-layer basis. If you make the engine save it as a png (which is what changing the force png setting does), it goes based off the original image format.

I tried modifying the code so that if it saves as a webp image, it will first check if the image is already in RGB8 or RGBA8 format. If it's already in one of those formats, it will use that format. If it's not in one of those formats, then it will check the alpha on that layer like before. The old code used to convert it to RGB8 or RGBA8 format even if it was already in one of those formats.

However, even after changing that section of the code, it still changes formats, I couldn't find where this was at, but I'll keep searching. For now, if you change the previously mentioned setting, you can get it to work.
I've created a pull request to fix the issue

This still occurs in 4.5-beta3 and even the suggested workarounds do not help.

Yeah texture arrays are interesting and weird

> and use _exactly that and only that_, instead of all this guesswork from pixels

The image saving function guesses, which works really well for single images

However, the texture arrays split the image, then save each section separately, which could lead to different parts being saved with different formats.

I don’t know why they did it this way and I don’t know anyone that I could ask about this.
If all sections of your image have transparent pixels, I think it’ll save properly in any format without needing force_png.

> If all sections of your image have transparent pixels, I think it’ll save properly in any format without needing force_png. Yes, but it really must be each pixel, because apparently some sections will still count as opaque even if they have fully transparent pixels.
